clue.text: Can he end IRA gats? Hell, no! Je faux!

definitions.text: Can he end IRA gats? Hell, no! Je faux!

indicators.note: French for false: the preceding words are a false arrangement of the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A sceptic wonders whether one man can end the IRA's guns, and answers with a French shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: The Canadian general John de Chastelain chaired the body overseeing IRA weapons decommissioning, so the whole clue both defines him and, with 'faux' as anagram signal, spells him from the 23 letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: De Chastelain led the independent commission charged with verifying that the IRA put its weapons beyond use.

clue.text: 1 across countermanding order to "Turn left!"

indicators.note: to countermand an order is to give the opposite one, so left in the command is swapped for its opposite

parts.note: the command could be put as GO LEFT
RT is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A general overrules a drill instruction to wheel left.
explanation.walkthrough: Countermanding 'go left' gives 'go right', with right shortened to RT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Gort was the British field marshal commanding the expeditionary force in France in 1940, so he is a general.

clue.text: Close trap over Henry

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the word for trap is turned upwards

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone shuts a trap on a man called Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Near or close by in distance or time; an old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Goes over the same ground with cheap rollers

definitions.meaning: to go back over old material again, a figurative sense
remoulded tyres, sold more cheaply than new ones

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rollers' looks like hair curlers or waves; here it means wheels' tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is a tyre given new tread, and to retread is to cover old ground again.

clue.text: Give suspended sentence out of court

definitions.text: Give suspended sentence out of court

parts.words: Give suspended sentence out of court
parts.note: a suspended sentence sounds judicial, but here the punishment is hanging, imposed by a mob without any trial

explanation.definitionFit: To lynch is to execute someone, typically by hanging, without legal process.

clue.text: 1 across, speaking of that bush kangaroo with love

indicators.note: says the name of the kangaroo is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: Skippy the Bush Kangaroo was a 1960s Australian children's TV series
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A general mentions a TV kangaroo fondly.
explanation.walkthrough: Skippy, said aloud, gives the first part of the Roman's name, spelt SCIPI.
explanation.definitionFit: Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who defeated Hannibal at Zama.

clue.text: 1 across shot Lorna with a knife

definitions.meaning: Field Marshal Michael ..., head of the British Army in the 1970s
the villain ... Doone shoots Lorna at her wedding in Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
one who carves, or the large knife used for carving meat

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a British field marshal, the villain of Lorna Doone, and a carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a field marshal, to the Doone villain, and to the knife for slicing roasts.

clue.text: Swan with claw winning the endless contest

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

indicators.note: winning here means gaining or taking in, so the claw holds the next piece

parts.note: a talon is a bird's claw

indicators.note: the word the loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A swan uses its claw to win an unending competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentathlon is an athletic contest made up of five events.

clue.text: Resounded with a weaving of tapestries

indicators.note: weaving combines threads in new patterns, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something echoed as a tapestry was being woven.
explanation.walkthrough: Oudenarde (Oudenaarde) in Flanders was famous for its tapestries, which take the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oudenardes are tapestries woven at Oudenaarde in Flanders, named after the town like gobelins.

clue.text: One with no label needs Irish backing on the menu

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a label is a tag, so no label is NO TAG

explanation.surface: Someone without a name badge needs Irish support to get onto the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a ridged tube pasta, the sort of dish found listed on an Italian menu.

clue.text: Insurance company retreat over cut back

parts.note: the Pru is the familiar name for the Prudential insurance company

indicators.note: over signals that the word for retreat is turned round

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: An insurer withdraws after making cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune is to trim or cut back, as with a shrub or a budget.

clue.text: Royal Ballet star has somehow put on weight

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A ballet star has put on weight somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Frederick Ashton was the Royal Ballet's founding choreographer and later its director.

clue.text: See 1
1 across: is 'e involved with "Erewhon Revisited"?

indicators.note: to revisit something here is to go over its letters again in a new order

parts.note: the dropped-aitch form of is he, used as written

explanation.surface: Was a general mixed up with Samuel Butler's sequel novel?
explanation.walkthrough: Erewhon Revisited is a real novel by Samuel Butler, which disguises its title word as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was the American general who commanded the Allied invasion of Normandy.

clue.text: 1 across: setter's input, "Not poor Mr Gladstone's monicker, Your Majesty!"

indicators.note: input means the following pieces are put into the setter's word

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me, so setter's is MY

indicators.note: poor signals the word not is in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: Gladstone was nicknamed the GOM, the Grand Old Man
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A setter contributes a protest to the monarch about a nickname for a statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns 'Not' into ONT. The comma breaks the clue into pieces; 'Your Majesty' is the Queen's cipher, a crossword staple, not an address to the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Montgomery was the British general who won at El Alamein.

clue.text: Immoderate, but natural to snatch Dior creation

indicators.note: the word for natural grabs and holds the next letters

parts.note: innate means natural or inborn

indicators.note: a fashion creation turns Dior's letters into a new design

explanation.surface: It is natural to grab a Dior design, but excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means excessive, beyond reasonable limits, just as immoderate does.

clue.text: Barbarian drowning everyone in rising stream in India

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the whole is read upwards
the barbarian swallows up the word for everyone

parts.note: a Hun, one of the invading barbarians
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A barbarian drowns everyone in a swelling river in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A nullah is an Indian watercourse or ravine, often dry except in the rains.

clue.text: See 19
A nastier form of water supply

indicators.note: a form of something here is its letters given a new shape

explanation.surface: A nastier sort of water source.
explanation.walkthrough: An artesian well delivers water forced up under natural pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Artesian describes a well or water source fed by pressure from an underground aquifer.

clue.text: She saved her people from the Medes thereof

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the following words, running across their join

explanation.surface: A Bible-study question about a heroine of the Persian court and her nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters sits across 'Medes thereof'; she was the Jewish queen of the Persian king in the Book of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical queen interceded with King Ahasuerus to save the Jews from Haman's plot.

clue.text: 1 across taking a gander with energy out of ruined barn

indicators.note: taking means the look holds the scrambled barn inside it

parts.note: to take a gander is to have a look

indicators.note: a ruined barn is knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A general glances over a wrecked barn with some vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' here means made from, joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Brooke, Viscount Alanbrooke, was the British general who served as Chief of the Imperial General Staff in the Second World War.

clue.text: Man one buried in the poet's ground: this poet?

parts.note: he stands for a man

indicators.note: the one is buried in the ground, put inside it

parts.note: sod is turf or ground, and this poet wrote about working the soil
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man is buried in the soil a poet wrote about: is this him?
explanation.walkthrough: Hesiod's Works and Days is about farming, so the ground is fittingly his.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesiod was an early Greek poet, author of Works and Days and the Theogony.

clue.text: What owls do with goats outside English songfests

indicators.note: the two pieces sit on either side of the letter for English

parts.note: owls hoot
nannies are female goats

explanation.surface: Owls hoot and goats bleat around an Englishman at a folk festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal gathering with folk singing, a songfest.

clue.text: Cardinals hearing Teutonic rejections

indicators.note: hearing means the German refusals are heard rather than seen

parts.note: nein is German for no, so the rejections are neins

explanation.surface: Churchmen listen as Germans say no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinals' wants to be churchmen; here it means cardinal numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are counting numbers, and nine is one of them, so nines are cardinals.

clue.text: See 1 across
Bisexual part of the Channel Islands?

definitions.meaning: a hermaphrodite, having both male and female organs, shortened
one of the smaller Channel Islands, near Guernsey

explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British Crown dependencies off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Herm is an island in the Bailiwick of Guernsey and also a short form of hermaphrodite.

clue.text: You and I are backward? That takes the (ship's) biscuit!

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: backward means the word for are is read in reverse

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist, so are can be live

explanation.surface: An exclamation at foolishness: we are slow? That beats everything!
explanation.walkthrough: 'That takes the biscuit' sounds like outrage; the weevil infests ship's biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Weevils notoriously bored into the hard tack, or ship's biscuit, eaten by sailors.

clue.text: Not "Enigma Variations"? No, Monsieur, it's a tragedy

indicators.note: variations rework a theme, here the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A Frenchman insists a piece is not Elgar's work but a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, Monsieur' says M is taken out of the letters of NOT ENIGMA, which 'Variations' rearranges; Enigma Variations is Elgar's.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigone is Sophocles' tragedy about Oedipus's daughter.

clue.text: First twenty-four hours in King Henry's revolutionary capital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the king and Henry

parts.note: R, for Rex, is king
H for Henry

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round

parts.note: the first day is day one, DAY I

explanation.surface: The opening day under a king called Henry in a capital in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: One's on equal terms with another

definitions.text: One's on equal terms with another

parts.words: One's on equal terms with another
parts.note: sounds like a person level with a rival, but means a word with the same meaning as another word

explanation.definitionFit: A word sharing its meaning with another word stands on equal terms with it in sense.
